label: Battle of Actium in Weigall's Life and Times of Cleopatra

source.edition: Edinburgh and London: William Blackwood and Sons, 1914

guidance: This is a modern historian's work, not an ancient source. Draft as claims what the author states about the people, forces, places, and events in scope.

Where the author reads an event as an instance of an in-scope concept, draft exemplifies; where the author presents a long-range consequence of it, draft ledTo. Record any other reading of what the events meant as a note of type interpretation.

For participatedIn, a person counts as taking part in the event when the passage shows them present during it: commanding, fighting, aboard a ship in the action, or fleeing from it. Preparations before the event, or the actions of a person's ships or troops with no sign of the person, do not by themselves show that the person took part.

commanded relates a person to a force they directed in action, using the force entities in scope: a fleet, one wing or the centre of a fleet, a squadron, or a land army. Command of a wing or the centre is not command of the whole fleet; use the most specific force the passage supports.

heldAuthorityOver is formal or supreme authority over a force, whether or not the person directed it in the fighting, for example an overall commander whose subordinate leads a wing. Draft it when the passage shows that authority, with a time only if the passage gives one.
The in-scope entity Augustus is the person modern authors usually call Octavian before 27 BCE. Decide from context whom the author means by Caesar.

Give a time in the author's own words as the time expression, only for predicates that take a time; add time_edtf only when the passage states the year. The author's footnotes and any transcriber's notes are not the passage text.
